mainTopic: Sight recognition versus identifying marks, and the laws of removing and eating the גיד הנשה
overview: The amud opens with a speaker changing his mind. He used to think סימנים were stronger than טביעות עינא. After hearing the rulings about meat and תכלת, he now says recognition by sight is stronger. He proves it from a blind man and from husbands at night, who know their wives by voice. רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא adds a proof from witnesses in a murder case, and רב אשי adds one from a man sending a messenger. Then a new משנה begins about the גיד הנשה. It discusses how much of the nerve must be removed, and how many lashes a person gets for eating it. The גמרא tells how שמואל rebuked בר פיולי for not cutting deep enough, and רב ששת explains what בר פיולי left behind. Finally, שמואל teaches that the Torah forbids only the part of the nerve on the כף הירך. רב פפא links this to a dispute between תנאים, whose reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Changing his mind: recognition by sight is stronger
steps.stepSummary: The speaker finishes his old view, that a lost object is not returned through טביעות עינא. Then he says that after hearing the recent rulings, he now holds that טביעות עינא is stronger than סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we do not return a lost object based on recognizing it by sight. But now that I have heard these rulings, I say that recognizing by sight is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker finishes describing his old view and then announces that he has changed his mind: recognizing something by sight is better than identifying marks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His old view came from the laws of lost objects, where only סימנים get an item returned. 'These rulings' are the earlier cases of meat and תכלת that went out of sight and were still allowed because someone recognized them. Those cases showed him that sight recognition is trusted even without marks.

keyTerms.meaning: Recognizing something by sight, knowing it just from how it looks
We return (a lost object to its owner)
Is better / is stronger
Rulings or teachings

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is saying lost objects are now returned through טביעות עינא. That rule is part of his old reasoning. What changes is his view of which kind of evidence is stronger in general.

phrases.english: and we do not return [a lost object] based on visual recognition.
Now that I have heard these rulings,
phrases.notes: He means the earlier rulings about meat and תכלת that were out of sight and were still allowed because they were recognized.

phrases.english: I say: visual recognition is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes and reverses the speaker's earlier opinion, which began before this text, that סימנים are stronger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טביעות עינא is a stronger form of identification than סימנים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main claim of the passage. Every step after it is a proof for it.

steps.title: Proof from a blind man and from husbands at night
steps.stepSummary: If recognition without marks were not trusted, a blind man could not be with his wife, and no man could be with his wife in the dark. They are allowed because they recognize her voice, so recognition works here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, how is a blind man allowed to be with his wife, and how are men allowed to be with their wives at night? It must be that they recognize them by voice. Here too, recognition by sight is trusted.
steps.whatsHappening: The speaker gives a strong proof from everyday life that recognition works even when no identifying marks can be seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blind man, or anyone in the dark, cannot check his wife's סימנים. He knows her only by her voice. Since the הלכה clearly allows this, recognizing someone without marks must be trusted, so recognition by sight works for the meat and the תכלת as well.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say so: introduces a proof showing that the other view leads to an impossible result
A blind person
Recognizing a voice, knowing someone by the sound of their voice
Here too: applies the same reasoning to our case

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
how is a blind man permitted to his wife,
phrases.notes: 'Permitted to his wife' means allowed to be intimate with her, even though he cannot see her to be sure it is her.

phrases.aramaic: וּבְנֵי אָדָם אֵיךְ מוּתָּרִין בִּנְשׁוֹתֵיהֶן בַּלַּיְלָה?
phrases.english: and how are people permitted to their wives at night?
Rather, it is through recognition of the voice,
here too, it is through visual recognition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the new claim in step 1 with a proof from everyday הלכה.
steps.raayaObject: That recognition without identifying marks is reliable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A blind man, and every husband at night, is allowed to be with his wife based only on recognizing her voice.

steps.title: Proof from witnesses in a murder case
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב משרשיא points out that a court would not execute someone based on witnesses describing his marks. It would execute him if the witnesses say they recognize him by sight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק son of רב משרשיא said: Know that this is true. If two witnesses come and say, 'So-and-so, who has this mark and that mark, killed a person,' we do not execute him. But if they say, 'We recognize him by sight,' we do execute him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא adds another proof: in capital cases, the court relies on recognition by sight but not on identifying marks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Capital cases need the strongest possible certainty. Since a court is willing to execute someone based on טביעות עינא but not based on סימנים, sight recognition must be the more reliable of the two.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that this is so): introduces a supporting proof
His identifying marks
So-and-so, a certain person
Killed a person

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Mesharshiyya, said:
Know [that this is so], for if two [witnesses] come and say:
So-and-so, who has this mark and that mark,
killed a person, we do not execute him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ אָמְרִי: אִית לַן טְבִיעוּת עֵינָא בְּגַוֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: whereas if they say: We recognize him by sight,
we execute him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate proof for the claim in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That טביעות עינא is stronger than סימנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Court procedure in capital cases: the court executes based on witnesses' sight recognition, but not based on a description of marks.

steps.title: Proof from sending a messenger to call someone
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי notes that a messenger told to call a person described by marks may or may not find the right one. If the messenger knows the person by sight, he will recognize him the moment he sees him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Know that this is true. If a man tells his messenger, 'Call so-and-so, who has this mark and that mark,' maybe the messenger will know him and maybe he will not. But if he recognizes him by sight, as soon as he sees him he knows him.
steps.whatsHappening: A third proof, this time from ordinary daily life, closes the passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A description by marks leaves room for doubt, because many people may fit it. Recognizing someone by sight gives immediate certainty. Ordinary experience therefore shows that טביעות עינא is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: His messenger
Uncertain, maybe yes and maybe no
When he sees him

steps.whatToRemember: The final view here is that טביעות עינא is stronger than סימנים. It is proven from a husband who knows his wife by voice, from witnesses in murder cases, and from a messenger calling someone.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע, דְּאִילּוּ אָמַר לֵיהּ אִינִישׁ לִשְׁלוּחֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Know [that this is so], for if a person says to his messenger:

phrases.aramaic: קַרְיֵיהּ לִפְלָנְיָא, דְּהַאי סִימָנֵיהּ וְהַאי סִימָנֵיהּ –
phrases.english: Call so-and-so, who has this mark and that mark,

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק יָדַע לֵיהּ, סָפֵק לָא יָדַע לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: maybe he will know him, maybe he will not know him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ אִית לֵיהּ טְבִיעוּת עֵינָא בְּגַוֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: whereas if he recognizes him by sight,
when he sees him, he knows him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע, דְּאִילּוּ אָמַר לֵיהּ אִינִישׁ לִשְׁלוּחֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third proof, from everyday experience, which closes the run of proofs.
steps.raayaObject: That טביעות עינא is stronger than סימנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Everyday experience: a messenger working from a description may get it wrong, but someone who knows the person by sight recognizes him at once.

steps.title: How much of the sciatic nerve must be removed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that whoever removes the גיד הנשה must remove all of it. רבי יהודה says it is enough to remove it in a way that fulfills the מצוה of removal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who removes the גיד הנשה must take out the whole thing. רבי יהודה says it is enough to remove it so that the מצוה of removal is done.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here. It presents a disagreement about how thoroughly the גיד הנשה must be removed from the animal's leg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא demands complete removal, which means digging into the surrounding meat to get every bit. רבי יהודה sets a lower bar: a basic removal that counts as doing the מצוה is enough, even if some thin parts stay behind.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
The sciatic nerve in an animal's hind leg, which the Torah forbids eating
Removal; here, cutting the nerve out of the meat
The requirement to remove the nerve, done in a basic acceptable way

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא's story right after this depends on this מחלוקת. שמואל follows the תנא קמא, and בר פיולי was trained like רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who removes the sciatic nerve
must remove all of it.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Enough to fulfill with it the מצוה of removal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹטֵל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּטּוֹל אֶת כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the earlier discussion of טביעות עינא ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא requires removing the entire nerve. רבי יהודה requires only enough removal to fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: Lashes for eating the sciatic nerve
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that eating a כזית of the גיד הנשה gets forty lashes. Eating a whole nerve smaller than a כזית also makes one liable. Eating a כזית from each leg gets eighty, but רבי יהודה says only forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone eats a כזית of the גיד הנשה, he gets forty lashes. If he eats a whole nerve that is less than a כזית, he is still liable. If he eats a כזית from this leg's nerve and a כזית from the other leg's nerve, he gets eighty lashes. רבי יהודה says he gets only forty.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and turns from removing the nerve to the punishment for eating it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three cases. A normal כזית gets the usual forty lashes. A whole nerve counts even below the normal amount, because it is a complete item. Two כזיתים from the two legs count as two separate violations, so the punishment is eighty. רבי יהודה disagrees and gives only forty for that last case.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume; the usual minimum amount for being punished for eating
Receives forty lashes, meaning the standard Torah punishment of lashes
Liable to punishment
Eighty, meaning two sets of lashes

steps.confusionAlert: The 'forty' lashes are the standard name for the Torah punishment of מלקות. Don't count them literally here. The key point is one set of lashes versus two.

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹכֵל מִגִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה כְּזַיִת – סוֹפֵג אַרְבָּעִים.
phrases.english: One who eats an olive-bulk of the sciatic nerve incurs forty lashes.
If he ate it whole and it is not an olive-bulk, he is liable.
phrases.notes: 'It' means a whole nerve. Since it's a complete item, size doesn't matter here.

phrases.english: If he ate an olive-bulk from this one and an olive-bulk from that one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' and 'that one' are the nerves of the right leg and the left leg.

phrases.english: he incurs eighty lashes.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סוֹפֵג אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעִים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He incurs only forty.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹכֵל מִגִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה כְּזַיִת – סוֹפֵג אַרְבָּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from removing the nerve to eating it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כזית gets forty lashes. A whole nerve under a כזית still makes one liable. A כזית from each leg gets eighty according to the תנא קמא, and only forty according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: שמואל rebukes בר פיולי for cutting too shallow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells how בר פיולי was removing the nerve in front of שמואל without cutting deep enough. שמואל told him to dig deeper and said that otherwise he would have fed him forbidden food.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פיולי was standing before שמואל and removing the nerve from a leg of meat. He was cutting it out only on the surface. שמואל said to him: 'Dig deeper! If I hadn't been watching you, you would have fed me something forbidden!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a real-life story that shows the מחלוקת of the משנה in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פיולי was removing the nerve the way רבי יהודה allows, with only a basic cut. שמואל holds like the תנא קמא, who requires removing all of it, so to him the leftover bits were still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה; marks the start of that discussion
Removing forbidden parts, such as the nerve or fats, from meat
Thigh or leg of an animal
Go down deeper into it; cut further
Something forbidden

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר פָּיוֹלֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: Bar Peyoli was standing before Shmuel,
and was removing the nerve from a leg.
He was cutting it out only on the surface.
He said to him: Go down deeper into it.

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא לָא חֲזֵיתָךְ – סְפֵית לִי אִיסּוּרָא!
phrases.english: Now, had I not seen you, you would have fed me something forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר פָּיוֹלֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the first מחלוקת of the משנה, about how much to remove, in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל requires removing the nerve completely, like the תנא קמא.

steps.title: שמואל reassures him: you were taught like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: בר פיולי was frightened and dropped his knife. שמואל calmed him, explaining that whoever taught him had taught him according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פיולי got scared, and the knife fell from his hand. שמואל said to him: 'Don't be afraid. Whoever taught you taught you like רבי יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל softens his strong rebuke. He explains that בר פיולי was not careless; he was following a real opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's harsh words made it sound as if בר פיולי was feeding people forbidden food. Here שמואל clarifies that בר פיולי's method is רבי יהודה's view in the משנה. שמואל himself still holds like the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: He trembled; he became afraid
Knife
Taught or ruled for; gave a halachic instruction

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה argues about whether the whole גיד הנשה must be removed. שמואל holds like the תנא קמא, that all of it must be removed. Removing only enough for the מצוה is רבי יהודה's view.

phrases.english: He became afraid, and the knife fell from his hand.
He said to him: Do not be afraid.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאוֹרִי לָךְ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹרִי לָךְ.
phrases.english: The one who taught you taught you in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּירְתַת, דְּאוֹרִי לָךְ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹרִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension from step 7 by explaining what בר פיולי was relying on.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the source of the practice: it follows רבי יהודה's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בר פיולי was careless or ignorant, and was feeding people forbidden food.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was following his teacher, who ruled like רבי יהודה. שמואל rules like the תנא קמא.

steps.title: רב ששת's first explanation of בר פיולי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says בר פיולי removed the part that is forbidden מדאורייתא according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What בר פיולי took out was the part forbidden by Torah law, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת is trying to explain exactly what בר פיולי did when he did not cut deep enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל had said that בר פיולי's teacher followed רבי יהודה. רב ששת now explains this: בר פיולי did remove everything that רבי יהודה says is forbidden by the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah itself; a Torah-level law
Took, removed

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
What bar Peyoli removed
was the part forbidden by Torah law, according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי דִּשְׁקַל בַּר פָּיוֹלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains שמואל's comment that בר פיולי's teacher followed רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר פיולי removed the Torah-level part of the nerve according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Then he left a rabbinic part behind
steps.stepSummary: If he removed only the Torah-level part per רבי יהודה, he must have left the rabbinic-level part per רבי יהודה. So whose opinion was his teacher following?
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that what he left behind was the part forbidden by rabbinic law, according to רבי יהודה. But then, according to whom did the one who taught him teach him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת's first explanation by showing what it would imply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בר פיולי left behind something that even רבי יהודה forbids מדרבנן, then he did something wrong even according to רבי יהודה. So it would be wrong to say his teacher taught him like רבי יהודה, and the teacher fits no opinion at all.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; it follows from this
Left over, left behind
From the Rabbis; a rabbinic-level law
Taught, gave a ruling

phrases.english: This implies that what he left behind
was the part forbidden by rabbinic law, according to Rabbi Yehuda.
But then, the one who taught him,
according to whom did he teach him?
phrases.notes: In other words, his teacher would not match anyone, since even רבי יהודה forbids that leftover part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's first explanation by drawing out what it implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that בר פיולי removed the Torah-level part according to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying he removed only the Torah-level part implies he left a rabbinic-level part, which even רבי יהודה forbids. Then the teacher matched no opinion, and שמואל's comment would not make sense.

steps.title: רב ששת's corrected explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that בר פיולי removed the Torah-level part, and what he left is forbidden only מדרבנן according to רבי מאיר. According to רבי יהודה, it is fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ששת said: What בר פיולי removed was the Torah-level part, and what he left behind is forbidden by rabbinic law according to רבי מאיר. But according to רבי יהודה, it is permitted even by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates רב ששת's words in a corrected form that avoids the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftover part is forbidden only by רבי מאיר, and only מדרבנן. רבי יהודה permits it completely. So the teacher really did follow רבי יהודה, just as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces a new answer that replaces the old one
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: בר פיולי's teacher followed רבי יהודה, who permits the leftover part completely. Only רבי מאיר forbids it, and only מדרבנן.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said:
What bar Peyoli removed was the Torah-level part,
and what he left behind is rabbinic, according to Rabbi Meir;
for if we follow Rabbi Yehuda,
it is permitted even by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַאי דִּשְׁקַל בַּר פָּיוֹלֵי – דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וּמַאי דְּשַׁיַּיר – דְּרַבָּנַן, לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the first explanation, which was challenged in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-explains the case: the leftover is rabbinic only according to רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leftover part was forbidden מדרבנן even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leftover part is forbidden מדרבנן only according to רבי מאיר; רבי יהודה permits it completely, so the teacher followed רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The Torah forbids only the part on the 'spoon'
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the משנה, שמואל says the Torah forbids only the part of the גיד הנשה that lies on the כף הירך, based on the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One who eats from the גיד הנשה, etc. שמואל said: The Torah forbade only the part that is on the 'spoon' of the thigh, as it says: 'on the spoon of the thigh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about eating the גיד הנשה and brings שמואל's teaching on which part the Torah forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the nerve is 'על כף הירך,' on the rounded part of the thigh. שמואל learns from this wording that only the section of the nerve lying on that spot is forbidden by the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
The rounded, spoon-shaped part of the thigh
Only

phrases.english: "One who eats from the sciatic nerve," etc.
Shmuel said:
The Torah forbade only
the part that is on the 'spoon' alone,
as it is stated: "on the spoon of the thigh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בר פיולי discussion and returns to the משנה about eating the nerve.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the part of the גיד הנשה on the כף הירך is forbidden by the Torah.

steps.title: שמואל's rule matches a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says שמואל's rule is connected to an argument between תנאים. The first view holds a person is liable for eating a whole nerve smaller than a כזית, and רבי יהודה says he is liable only for a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is like a dispute between תנאים. If one ate it and it did not contain a כזית, he is liable. רבי יהודה says: He is not liable unless it contains a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא says שמואל's statement depends on an older argument between תנאים, and he quotes that argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view holds that eating a whole nerve makes one liable even if it is smaller than a כזית. רבי יהודה says you are liable only for a full כזית. רב פפא says שמואל's rule matches one side of this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: This matches a dispute between תנאים
An olive-sized amount, the minimum amount of eating that brings a punishment
Liable, here to receive lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier the משנה (Step 6) said a whole nerve smaller than a כזית makes one liable. Here רבי יהודה disagrees and requires a full כזית.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is like a dispute between tanna'im:
If one ate it and it did not contain an olive-bulk, he is liable.
phrases.notes: "It" means a whole nerve, eaten all together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not until it contains an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects שמואל's rule to an earlier argument between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל's rule matches one side of a dispute between תנאים about a whole nerve smaller than a כזית.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן make him liable for less than a כזית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the רבנן's view that eating a whole nerve smaller than a כזית makes a person liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן hold a person liable for eating a whole גיד הנשה that is smaller than a כזית. It is setting up the explanation that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person is only liable for eating a forbidden food if he eats at least a כזית. The רבנן in step 13 seem to break that rule, so the גמרא wants to know what makes this case different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The Sages; here, the first view in the argument from step 13
An olive's size, the usual minimum amount for being liable for eating

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: "The Rabbis" are the first view from step 13, who say he is liable even for a whole nerve smaller than an olive's size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the first view quoted by רב פפא in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the רבנן make a person liable for eating a whole גיד הנשה smaller than a כזית, against the usual כזית minimum.

steps.title: The nerve is a complete creation on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גיד הנשה is a בריה, a complete creation, so eating the whole thing makes a person liable even if it is less than a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a complete creation on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן see the גיד הנשה as a בריה, a whole, complete thing in its own right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person eats something whole and complete, that eating counts as important even if it is smaller than a כזית. So the רבנן do not need the כזית amount here. רבי יהודה, who requires a כזית, does not treat the nerve this way. How this connects to שמואל's rule from step 12 is explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A complete creation, a whole thing that stands as its own unit
On its own, by itself
The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids us to eat

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן make a person liable for a whole גיד הנשה smaller than a כזית because it is a בריה, a complete creation, and eating a whole thing counts even below the usual amount.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the כזית rule in general. It is a special exception for something whole, a בריה.

phrases.english: It is a complete creation (on its own).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; either way the point is that the nerve is a whole thing by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by giving the reasoning of the רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גיד הנשה is a בריה, a complete creation, so eating it whole makes a person liable even without a כזית.
